clue.text: See 12
Brother or sister left some flowers outside, perhaps

indicators.note: the bunch of flowers is placed outside, wrapping round the sibling and the left

parts.note: a posy is a small bunch of flowers
a sib is a sibling, brother or sister

explanation.surface: A sibling leaves a bunch of flowers outside, maybe on a doorstep.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words express that something may be so without certainty; they are interchangeable adverbs.

clue.text: Mend one's ways, as the 24 never did

definitions.meaning: to improve one's conduct, turn over a new leaf
the 24-across band split in 1970 and never got back together as a group

explanation.walkthrough: 24 is the answer to 24 across, the Fab Four, who famously never regrouped after breaking up.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to improve behaviour and, of a band, to get back together after splitting.

clue.text: Serviceman agrees about not losing heart

indicators.note: about signals the letters of agrees being turned around into a new order
losing heart strips the middle letter from not, leaving just its ends

explanation.surface: A soldier gives his assent, though without much enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges AGREES to SERGEA; 'losing heart' takes the middle O out of NOT, giving NT.
explanation.definitionFit: A sergeant is a non-commissioned rank in the army or air force, so a serviceman.

clue.text: Art of jazz? It could be green, red or yellow

definitions.text: It could be green, red or yellow
definitions.meaning: the capsicum vegetable comes in green, red and yellow varieties

explanation.walkthrough: 'Art' looks like a common noun but is the jazzman's first name; the answer also completes the Sgt ___ album title.
explanation.definitionFit: Art Pepper the saxophonist shares his surname with the bell vegetable sold in several colours.

clue.text: Take supporting role in film

definitions.meaning: to assist someone, play second fiddle
the 1965 Beatles film with an exclamation mark in its title

explanation.definitionFit: To assist is to aid someone, and it is also the title of the 1965 Fab Four movie.

clue.text: O.J. once trained with small Spanish balls

indicators.note: trained suggests the letters are drilled and put into a different formation

parts.note: the initials O and J, taken without their full stops
taken as written
S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: O.J. Simpson once practised with little balls in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trained' rearranges OJ and ONCE into COJONE, and S is added on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish slang word for testicles, also borrowed in English for nerve or guts.

clue.text: Ultimately extract revenge, executed cruelly?

indicators.note: cruelly suggests violent mangling, so the remaining letters are jumbled
ultimately points to the final letter of the following word extract
executed means beheaded, so the word revenge loses its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone finally takes vengeance, carried out with great brutality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ultimately' gives T; 'executed' beheads REVENGE to EVENGE; 'cruelly' rearranges T plus EVENGE. The whole clue also describes the act, so it is an &lit.
explanation.definitionFit: To get one's own back is to take revenge, which is exactly what the clue's surface describes.

clue.text: File name lacking appeal for poetry

indicators.note: lacking means the second word's letters are missing from the first

parts.note: The Odessa File is a Frederick Forsyth thriller, so Odessa is the name of a file
SA is short for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A computer file is lacking any appeal, so it's filed under verse.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing SA from ODESSA, the name in Forsyth's novel title The Odessa File, leaves the poems.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyric poems addressed to a subject, so collectively they are poetry; plural noun for a mass noun.

clue.text: Seed new grape — 80% Pinot

indicators.note: new implies the letters are given a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: eighty per cent of a five-letter word keeps its first four letters

explanation.surface: A wine label: a fresh grape blend that is four-fifths Pinot.
explanation.walkthrough: '80%' cuts PINOT to PINO; 'new' rearranges GRAPE plus PINO.
explanation.definitionFit: The small seed found inside citrus fruit, typically spat out or used for growing.

clue.text: "Dreadful waster" son has as name

indicators.note: dreadful signals that the letters are in a terrible mess and must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A father's son is known by the nickname 'Dreadful waster'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dreadful' rearranges WASTER and SON together.
explanation.definitionFit: To respond to a given name is to be called by it, an idiomatic phrase.

clue.text: Book mostly 14 ab ovo

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word is kept, here dropping its closing two letters

parts.note: 14 is white, and ab ovo is Latin for from the egg, so egg white, which is albumen

explanation.surface: A Latin tag about starting from the very beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ab ovo' usually means 'from the beginning' but here is literal: white from the egg. The answer also completes the White ___ theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A blank book for photographs or stamps, and also a record collection.

clue.text: London landmark in 15 board game

indicators.note: game suggests playing with the letters and moving them around

parts.note: the answer to 15 across, the online auction website
taken as written

explanation.surface: A London tourist spot features in an online board game sold at auction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' rearranges EBAY (15 across) with BOARD. The zebra crossing in St John's Wood is famous from the album cover.
explanation.definitionFit: The St John's Wood street with its recording studios and zebra crossing is a London sight.

clue.text: Birds' standard recipe — pig out with seconds

indicators.note: out places the pig outside, wrapping round the other pieces

parts.note: a sow is a female pig
par is a standard or norm, as in golf
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin, on prescriptions

explanation.surface: Bird's custard recipe tells you to eat greedily and take second helpings.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes Bird's custard, a British dessert brand; 'Birds'' is in fact the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Small brown passerine songbirds are common examples of birds; a hyponym.

clue.text: Ball the West Indies' opener hit for six

indicators.note: a cricket phrase for being knocked about, so the letters are scattered

parts.note: taken as written
WI is the standard abbreviation for the West Indies cricket team

explanation.surface: A cricket report: the West Indies batsman smashes a ball out of the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hit for six' rearranges THE with WI. In cricket, hitting for six means striking the ball over the boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: The cue ball in snooker is the white, and day-night cricket uses a white ball too.

clue.text: Play a 24 clip back where lots are online?

indicators.note: back means the extracted letters are read in the other direction
a clip is a small extract, so a short run of letters is taken from the words

parts.note: play a, followed by the answer to 24 across, the Liverpool band

explanation.surface: An instruction to play a short excerpt of a band's song backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clip' takes YABE from plaY A BEatles and 'back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: The online auction site where items, or lots, are bid on; the question mark flags the pun on lots.

clue.text: Butler maybe ordering her Times

indicators.note: ordering means putting the letters into a different order

parts.note: T is an abbreviation for time, so two Ts for times

explanation.surface: A butler perhaps sorting out her copy of The Times newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordering' rearranges HER into RHE. 'Butler' looks like a manservant but is a surname.
explanation.definitionFit: The forename of the hero Butler in Gone with the Wind, so an example of a Butler.

clue.text: Eg "Top Gun"

parts.note: not the film: a gun that spins like a top, a handgun with a rotating cylinder

explanation.walkthrough: The film title is a red herring; read 'Top Gun' as a firearm with a spinning part. It is also a Beatles album.
explanation.definitionFit: A handgun with a revolving chamber turns like a spinning top, hence a top gun.

clue.text: Note start of chart success

indicators.note: start of picks out the first letter of the next word chart

parts.note: a hit is a success, especially a chart-topping record

explanation.surface: A remark about the beginning of a record's chart success.
explanation.definitionFit: A short written note or voucher, such as an IOU, is a chit.

clue.text: A little bit of fine silk can set off leather

indicators.note: set off suggests the letters are disturbed and rearranged
a little bit of the word fine is just its first letter

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A small amount of quality silk can enhance a leather outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A little bit of' gives F; 'set off' rearranges F, SILK and CAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine leather made from the hide of a young cow is a type of leather.

clue.text: Where flowers are put next to wine for Max?

parts.note: by means beside or next to
Graves is a Bordeaux wine region and its wine

explanation.surface: Asking where mourners leave flowers, set beside a bottle of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Where flowers are put' is a second cryptic reading: by graves. Max Bygraves was a British comedian and singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Bygraves was a popular British entertainer, so Max is his first name.

clue.text: Turn from pet? A tortoise doing somersault!

indicators.note: a somersault flips over, so the letters are read backwards
from indicates the letters are drawn out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A pet tortoise performing a somersault, turning head over heels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' takes ETATOR from petA TORtoise; 'doing somersault' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To spin round on an axis is to turn; the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Bohemian poet O'Reilly knew but regularly ignored

indicators.note: every other letter is ignored, so the alternate letters remain

explanation.surface: O'Reilly knew the poet but regularly ignored him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly ignored' drops the odd letters of O'REILLY KNEW, leaving the even ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Rainer Maria Rilke was born in Prague, in Bohemia, and wrote poetry in German.

clue.text: A sport informally allowing change of centre pairing for series of games

indicators.note: the two middle letters of the word are swapped out for a different pair

parts.note: rugger is informal British slang for rugby union

explanation.surface: A sport that informally lets players switch partners in the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: The central GG of RUGGER becomes BB. Rugby union is called rugger informally in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge or tennis a rubber is a set of games, a series decided by the majority.

clue.text: Soldiers entertained by Spice Girl? Ring doctor — one may go into shock

indicators.note: being entertained by someone puts the soldiers inside their host

parts.note: Mel C, Sporty Spice, of the Spice Girls
TA is the Territorial Army
O is ring-shaped
MB is a Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor

explanation.surface: Troops are hosted by a pop star, then someone calls a medic for treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shock' here means a shock of hair, not trauma; the question mark on 'Spice Girl?' hints at Mel C.
explanation.definitionFit: A comb made of metal is pulled through a shock, a thick mass of hair.

clue.text: "Come Together"? That's fitting

definitions.meaning: to assemble or gather, also a Beatles song title
proper or appropriate, an old adjective sense

explanation.definitionFit: To gather is to assemble, and as an adjective the word means suitable or proper.

clue.text: Music primarily suggesting one setter's no old man

indicators.note: primarily gives the first letter of the next word suggesting

parts.note: O resembles the figure zero, here read as one letter

indicators.note: no says the old man is missing from the setter's name

parts.note: the setter Puck's real name is Paul
pa is an informal word for father, an old man

explanation.surface: A setter admits he's no father figure, with music suggesting one.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter of this puzzle, Puck, is named Paul; taking PA out leaves UL.
explanation.definitionFit: A genre of African-American popular music rooted in gospel and rhythm and blues.

clue.text: I'm not sure what the pong might be, boss!

parts.note: um is the noise of hesitation
BO is body odour, a pong

explanation.surface: Someone sniffing the air and asking their boss what the smell could be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pong' is British slang for a smell. 'boss' is not a manager but the raised centre of a shield.
explanation.definitionFit: The central raised knob of a shield is called its boss.

clue.text: Attend LSE, masquerading as producers of featured works

parts.note: to be at an event is to attend it

indicators.note: masquerading means disguising, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Going to the London School of Economics in disguise.
explanation.walkthrough: LSE is the London School of Economics. 'masquerading' rearranges LSE into LES. The featured works are the albums in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: The Fab Four recorded the albums that appear throughout this grid, so they produced them.

clue.text: Clashing belt and tie? Don't change a thing

indicators.note: clashing suggests things that do not go together, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Belt and tie clash, but leave them as they are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clashing' rearranges BELT and TIE.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom telling someone to leave things alone, a Beatles song and album title.
